effect.sample_note: Single official run scored by the challenge evaluator; the interval is a point, not a confidence interval. Observed same-content rerun spread is about +/-130bp (byte-identical candidates scored 2.9042110287045, 2.8930596055435216 and 2.86645713502766), so a verdict is only recorded as improved or regressed when the delta exceeds that spread.

nodes.summary: An exact recovery of a public parity-passing candidate. The submitted content is byte-identical to the promoted PR #234 tree, and it scored 130 basis points lower. There is no mechanism here: this is the evaluator measuring the same code twice and disagreeing with itself by 1.3 percent. Every other effect in this graph should be read against this number.

nodes.summary: Officially promoted: it beat the standing crown and became the new base. The measured delta is +3 basis points, which is roughly forty times smaller than the observed same-content rerun spread. Promotion here means 'ranked above the incumbent on one run', not 'measured to help'. The campaign nonetheless treats it as a proven complementary component because it is exact, tiny, and never measured negative. This is the clearest case in the corpus of a promotion that carries no resolved effect.

nodes.summary: Retiling the gated-delta recurrence at value dimension 64 for two widths. All eight pairs passed. The measured whole-run delta is minus two basis points against its own submission-time base: the local isolated recurrence ratios were real and simply did not reach the ranked score. An isolated kernel improvement that produces a null whole-run result is the most common failure shape in this campaign.

nodes.summary: The campaign's largest clean official gain. Every tensor of the incumbent Q4/group-64 head is preserved byte for byte and six bare proposal-only BF16 tensors are added: K and V rows fully corrected, the 1,024 largest-error Q rows corrected, recovering 29.35 percent of incumbent Q reconstruction error. All official fidelity gates passed. Note that the campaign ledger annotates this result as +5.11 percent, which does not follow from the two scores it quotes; the ratio of the quoted scores is +1.72 percent and that is what is recorded here.
